title: T4 layout gate RESULT: new libart (r1+T1 21 patches) vs board R155 libart — PASS
method: binary-to-binary (new libart built by T3, board R155 libart 59e1bb45). Layer A: image/oat version constants. Layer C: art_quick_* asm entrypoint offset immediates (asm_support offsets baked as ldr/str [xSELF,#imm]). GOT/global loads (adrp+ldr) and disasm-window overflow excluded (both were false positives caught during analysis).

layer_C_asm_offsets.named_anchors: MIRROR_OBJECT_CLASS_OFFSET=0, MIRROR_CLASS_COMPONENT_TYPE_OFFSET=12, THREAD_CARD_TABLE_OFFSET=152, THREAD_ID_OFFSET=8 — identical R155 vs NEW
layer_C_asm_offsets.thread_offset_set: 13 distinct Thread(x19) offsets, IDENTICAL across all 244 common art_quick entrypoints

false_positives_ruled_out: adrp+ldr GOT/global-data loads (e.g. ldr x16,[x16,#0xb58] after adrp) differ by data-section layout between two independently-linked binaries — NOT a struct offset; excluded (only x19/xSELF Thread accesses compared).
fixed-512-byte disasm window overflowed into neighbouring functions (method_exit_hook) capturing their offsets [16,96] — bounded to each symbol's actual size via nm --print-size.
verdict: T4 PASS: the new libart's mirror(6-class-relevant offsets) + Thread layout + image/oat versions match the board R155. => proceed to T5. The r16 image was rejected by CheckSystemClass because the r16 libart differs; the T1-reconstructed libart does NOT.
